synopsis: Tsutomu Yamaguchi remarkably survived both the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki in 1945, a unique and officially recognized feat.
narration: Tsutomu Yamaguchi, a Japanese engineer, endured what no one else officially did: surviving both the Hiroshima and Nagasaki atomic bombings in 1945. His extraordinary story of resilience was formally recognized in 2009, a testament to human survival against unimaginable odds.

shots.prompt: Medium shot of a Japanese man in his early 30s, dressed in a 1940s business suit, walking through a bustling, pre-war Hiroshima street. Sunlight is bright, people are going about their day. Suddenly, a blinding flash of white light fills the frame from behind him, followed by a violent shockwave distorting the scene. The man shields his eyes just as the world blurs into chaos. The camera simulates a brief, jarring shake.

Close-up of the same man, now haggard, wounded, and disoriented, stumbling through the desolate, ash-covered ruins of Nagasaki. Smoke drifts in the background. His clothes are torn, but his eyes show a profound, weary resilience and a glint of survival. He clutches a small, personal item. The camera slowly pulls back, revealing a landscape of utter devastation around him, emphasizing his solitary, enduring presence.

music: Somber and reflective yet with an underlying pulse of resilience and determination. Features a subtle, driving percussion and a poignant, ascending string motif. The intensity builds gently, reflecting survival and hope, and ends on a sustained, resonant note that cycles back.
